blogs.title: "Orthogonal Finetuning Unpacked – Rotating Neural Networks Without Overhauling Them"
blogs.description: "Large foundation models cost billions when trained from scratch; OT keeps pre-trained knowledge intact by multiplying each neuron’s weight vector with a small learnable orthonormal matrix—rotating feature space without changing angles between neurons—and reducing the number of extra parameters compared to full gradient updates.

blogs.title: "Butterfly Factorization – Borrowing From FFT To Build Dense Anticorrelated Matrices With Fewer Parameters"
blogs.description: "By viewing dense orthonormal matrices as messages transmitted across layers in an explicit forested network graph, researchers realized that stacking logarithmically many sparse ‘butterfly’ blocks reproduces any full rotation while needing only O(d log d) trainable values instead of O(d²). These blocks mirror stages from CooleyâTukey FFT where pairs interchange bits.’

blogs.title: "Real-world Impact Of BOFT – Fast Fine-Tuning Across Vision Transformers And Language Models"
blogs.description: "Replacing conventional LoRA modules with BOFT’s multiplicative butterfly layers achieves higher top-driven performance on ImageNet after STL-ViT adaptation and yields more coherent controlled images when applied to Stable Diffusion—all without increasing inference latency.”

blogs.title: "Why Preserving Spectral Norms Matters – The Hidden Advantage Of Orthogonality In Fine-Tuning"
blogs.description:
"Because every learned weight remains R·W⁰ where R stays strictly orthonormal during training, singular values stay unchanged compared to the frozen baseline.
This guarantees training trajectories never magnify gradients unexpectedly and simplifies regularisation.
It also reveals an elegant equivalence to learning bilinear similarities under hard rotation constraints.

blogs.title: "Beyond Butterfly Graphs – Future Directions For Structured Parameter Efficiency"
blogs.description:
"The success of butterfly layouts opens doors to exploring alternative network topologies (such as expander graphs or meshing patterns) capable of building even sparser yet expressive orthonormal maps.
Key research questions then involve faster backward propagation through chained sparse blocks,
a deeper theoretical understanding linking inductive bias to generalisation,
and crafting mixed-block designs that balance regularisation against expressive power.”
